dedupe_keys.name: climate risk and business ports terminal maritimo muelles el bosque cartagena colombia ifc 2011

description: A climate risk assessment by the International Finance Corporation of its client Terminal Marítimo Muelles El Bosque (MEB), a container terminal in Cartagena, Colombia, one of the first studies of IFC's Climate Risk and Adaptation Program begun in 2008. Coverage: one terminal plus a general review of climate risks for ports. Methods and contents: risks and opportunities are assessed across the terminal's activities, including vulnerability of its design and operations to sea level rise, flooding that disrupts movements and damages stored goods, reduced navigability of access channels, business interruption and changes in trade flows. Outcome: detailed data from MEB supported the design and operations assessments; wider economic effects rested on the literature; the report sets out climate-resilient actions the company could take. Format and access: free report (World Bank report 62641, April 2011) with an executive summary. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence was stated on the pages read. Caveats: a 2011 view of climate science and a single private terminal. Useful as a template for hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies of individual terminals. It relates to the Port of Los Angeles and Associated British Ports adaptation case studies in the catalogue.
